title: annotation mop-up notebook
content:
Quick brain dump for labeling cleanup + edge-case heuristics (personal notebook).

Context:
- This is a messy personal scratchpad for triaging ambiguous examples from the client chat logs dataset (v3).
- Goal: produce a compact set of deterministic heuristics we can hand off to contract annotators for a 2-hour mop-up run.
- Not a final guideline — includes unresolved questions and examples to escalate.

High-level rules (working):
1) Primary label precedence: intent > sentiment > out-of-scope.
   - If a message contains a clear instruction or request, mark as Intent:Command/Query even if sentiment negative.
2) Multi-intent: allow up to 2 primary intents. If >2, mark as MULTI_INTENT and add a short free-text note.
3) Sentiment only applies when message is evaluative about a product/person (positive/negative/neutral).
   - If there is sarcasm, use literal polarity unless sarcasm explicitly reverses sentiment and is obvious.
4) Spam/garbage: short gibberish (random characters, repeated emojis) => OUT_OF_SCOPE:spam.

Edge cases and examples (annotator-facing examples to clarify):
- "I hate that it crashes every 2 minutes, fix it."
  -> INTENT:BugReport, SENTIMENT:Negative (contains explicit request + complaint).
- "Can you check logs? It's been fine though"
  -> INTENT:Request:Check, SENTIMENT:Neutral (hedging phrase 'though' does not imply positive sentiment).
- "Thanks!" or "thx"
  -> INTENT:None, SENTIMENT:Positive (unless surrounding context flips meaning).
- "lol no way, that's great"
  -> INTENT:None, SENTIMENT:Positive (informal token 'lol' not sarcasm here).
- "Yeah, right... that worked well" (with ellipsis)
  -> If ellipsis + context suggests sarcasm, mark SENTIMENT:Negative and add NOTE:sarcastic. If ambiguous — mark SENTIMENT:Ambiguous and escalate.
- "Update: The dataset is ready — see attached"
  -> INTENT:Notification, SENTIMENT:Neutral, ATTACHMENT:Yes (if link detected).

Ambiguous intent heuristics (short):
- "I was wondering if you could" => INTENT:Request (polite phrasing still request).
- "Do you know why" => INTENT:Question:Why.
- "How do I" => INTENT:Instruction:HowTo.
- If "please" appears with a verb -> Request.

Label normalization notes:
- Use canonical labels (Intent:BugReport, Intent:FeatureRequest, Intent:HowTo, Intent:GeneralQuestion, Intent:AccountHelp, Intent:Billing, Out_of_scope, Spam).
- Sentiment canonical set: Positive / Neutral / Negative / Ambiguous.
- For multi-label fields separate values with a pipe character in CSV exports (e.g. BugReport|FeatureRequest).

Regex & quick filters to pre-tag (for triage):
- Billing / invoice regex: "\b(invoice|billing|charge|refund|receipt)\b" -> tag as POSSIBLE:Billing (send to humans for final).
- Account words: "\b(login|password|sign[- ]?in|account|reset)\b" -> POSSIBLE:AccountHelp.
- URLs/attachments: detect http(s): -> ATTACHMENT:Yes.

Common pitfalls observed (to warn annotators):
- Long conversational threads: label only the target message, not previous context unless instructed.
- Messages that are code snippets: treat as OUT_OF_SCOPE:technical-snippet unless the text outside the snippet is a request.
- Emoji-heavy replies: if emoji is the only content, infer sentiment from emoji (thumbs up = Positive, crying/loud-cry = Negative). If mixed emojis, mark Sentiment:Ambiguous.

Sampling of problematic real examples (redacted) + suggested labels: 
- "Ugh, why is this still broken? I've tried restarting 10 times." -> Intent:BugReport | Sentiment:Negative
- "If you could add a dark mode that'd be sick" -> Intent:FeatureRequest | Sentiment:Positive
- "8gj2k!!!" -> Out_of_scope:Spam
- "Can someone help me with my workspace? it just vanished" -> Intent:AccountHelp | Sentiment:Negative

Mop-up tasks (2-hour run):
- Top priority: Resolve label conflicts where two annotators disagreed (use majority vote; list below).
- Medium: Tag obvious spam/outliers and remove from active training set.
- Low: Add short notes for ambiguous sarcasm examples and escalate to product for rule decision.

Conflict list (examples to reconcile):
- Example IDs: DA-3451 (sarcasm), DA-3490 (multi-intent), DA-3503 (attachment flagged incorrectly).
  - Proposed: For DA-3451 -> mark Ambiguous + add NOTE:sarcasm?; escalate if >50 similar examples.
  - For DA-3490 -> allow two primary intents; if more, MULTI_INTENT.

Open questions / escalate to leads:
- Do we want to train on sarcasm-labeled data or exclude? (product/ops input needed — sarcasm often noisy)
- For multi-intent messages that map to two product teams, do we store both intents or pick primary? (ops prefers multi-intent storage)

Quick checklist for annotators (copyable):
- Read only the target message.
- Apply one or two intent labels max.
- Mark sentiment only if explicitly evaluative.
- Use OUT_OF_SCOPE for code-only, gibberish, irrelevant content.
- Add NOTE if sarcasm suspected.

TODO (me):
- Turn these heuristics into a short 1-page instruction sheet for the vendor.
- Create a small golden set (50 examples) with unanimous labels for QA.
- Run a regex pass to auto-flag likely billing/account messages and inspect precision.

Scratch ideas for automation:
- Use a lightweight classifier to pre-populate Intent:AccountHelp vs Billing, then humans validate.
- Emoji sentiment mapping table to reduce annotator ambiguity.
- Quick UI tweak: show preceding message timestamp + one prior message to help with context without overloading annotators.

Notes to self (fragments):
- Keep examples short in final guide.
- Remove technical jargon in vendor instructions.
- Make escalation path explicit (who to ping on Slack).

Slack refs / links to ticketing:
- Slack: #data-annotation (ping @samir for urgent edge-case adjudication).
- JIRA: JIRA-DA-678 = mop-up batch config + sampling.

End of dump. Will convert to polished doc after vendor call on Mon.
